html:
SMTO-EXE-0253 — Part of this task may not have finished, so it can't be saved yet

GUID: bce1613b-d357-52b7-ba1f-b3a17d9eb6bb
Slug: recipe-capture-contains-unknown-effect
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • While this task ran, at least one action ended without SMTO knowing whether it worked, or a question was left open. SMTO won't save a workflow from it until that's settled, so nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation and find the step marked as uncertain or failed. Note what it was trying to change, such as a file, message or setting. That step may already have made its change, even though SMTO couldn't confirm it.
  2. Check the result yourself, for example open the file or place it changed, or ask SMTO in the conversation to look without changing anything. Looking first is safe and stops the same change from being made twice.
  3. Only if the change did not happen, ask SMTO to finish it. Answer any question the task left open. SMTO saves workflows only from tasks with no unsettled actions or open questions.
  4. Then select Save to workflow on your original message and select Save workflow. Once nothing is uncertain, your request can be saved and reused.

What success looks like

  • The conversation shows no uncertain steps or open questions, and the workflow appears on the Workflows page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the whole task to clear this; it could repeat a change that already happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Workflow capture was rejected because the source run has unknown operations, open requirements, an outcome_unknown result, or a write that ran without a successful result.

What this means

  • Capture found unknown operations, open requirements, uncertain receipts or an executed write without successful evidence. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • Capture found unknown operations, open requirements, uncertain receipts or an executed write without successful evidence.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation receipts and open requirements; reconcile actual effects using fresh observations.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the source run's unknown_operations, open_requirements and operation results in the task state; settle each uncertain write by reading the target's current state, not by replaying it. Capture again only after recorder.extract finds no unresolved effect.
  • Resolve the original run's uncertain operations and requirements before recording; do not rerun writes to manufacture evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Resolve the original run's uncertain operations and requirements before recording; do not rerun writes to manufacture evidence.

How to verify the fix

  • The source run has no unresolved effects or open requirements and capture accepts its completion.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
